results.evidence: tests/test_prospects_reimport.py::test_reimporting_the_same_file_changes_nothing imports a valid two-record file (one direct_candidate, one relationship_prospect) twice. It asserts the second run exits 0 (EXIT_OK) and that stdout is exactly ['record 1 (acme-1): matched lead 1', 'record 2: matched lead 2', 'imported 0, matched 2, rejected 0']. It also asserts the row counts of organizations, contacts, leads, evidence and activities are unchanged after the second run. The whole file ran 14 passed. The summary format is produced at cottonwood/prospects.py:103. I could not run a separate manual CLI scenario because the sandbox blocked my scratch-file writes, so this rests on the test run and on reading the test.

_find_organization matches on domain_norm when the record has a domain, and on name_norm only when it has none. A domain that no stored organization has therefore creates a new organization even if the name matches. normalize_domain lowercases and strips 'www.', so 'WWW.Acme.com' becomes 'acme.com'. The three tests in tests/test_prospects_reimport.py cover the three clauses: test_domain_match_ignores_the_name, test_name_match_without_a_domain and test_unknown_domain_creates_an_organization_despite_a_name_match. All 14 tests in that file pass.

_find_contact (prospects.py) matches on email_norm with deleted_at IS NULL, and only when the record has no email falls back to normalized name within the same organization, also excluding deleted contacts. _find_lead matches on organization_id and type, comparing property locations with strip().casefold(), so ' 12 Main St ' equals '12 main st'. None and empty both become '' and match each other. Otherwise _import_one inserts a new lead. The parametrized test (' 12 Main St ' vs '12 main st' gives 1 lead, None vs None gives 1, '12 Main St' vs None gives 2, '12 Main St' vs '14 Main St' gives 2) and the contact tests for email, deleted_at and name within the same organization pass. All 14 tests in tests/test_prospects_reimport.py passed.

results.evidence: The test re-imports a matched record with one extra evidence item and organization.category changed from dental to orthodontics. It asserts that the row-count delta is organizations 0, contacts 0, leads 0, evidence 1, activities 1. It asserts that the stored lead, organization and contact rows are unchanged. It asserts the printed line "organization.category differs: stored 'dental', incoming 'orthodontics' (kept stored)", and that the new activity is of type 'imported'. The code at prospects.py:74-75 formats that message. All 14 tests in tests/test_prospects_reimport.py passed.

The test test_second_record_for_the_same_lead_in_one_file_is_matched imports a file with two records for the same lead. It asserts the first line is 'created lead 1', the second is 'matched lead 1', and the last line is 'imported 1, matched 1, rejected 0'. It also asserts one lead and one evidence row. I ran tests/test_prospects_reimport.py and all 14 tests passed. The summary format comes from cottonwood/prospects.py:103. I did not run the CLI by hand outside the tests.
